title: Separable descent of isotropy for diagonal p-forms
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] of prime characteristic $p>0$, let $L/k$ be an algebraic separable field extension (every element of $L$ is algebraic over $k$ and its minimal polynomial has distinct roots in an algebraic closure), and let $n\ge1$. For $1\le i\le n$ let $c_i\in k$ and $m_i\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$. If there is a tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in L^n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^n c_i a_i^{p^{m_i}}=0$, then there is a tuple $(b_1,\ldots,b_n)\in k^n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^n c_i b_i^{p^{m_i}}=0$. Coefficients $c_i=0$ and unequal exponents $m_i$ are allowed.

source.place: Lemma 1.12, printed p.7; for an arbitrary separable algebraic extension, apply the Galois assertion in a normal closure of the finite separable subextension generated by the coordinates. Read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf; local archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag is claimed.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois] choose a separable closure $\Omega/k$, which is Galois over $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed] embed $L$ into $\Omega$ over $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension] to the finite set of images of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ to obtain a finite Galois subextension $M/k$ containing those images. An embedding preserves the displayed equation and a nonzero coordinate. It therefore suffices to prove the assertion for every finite Galois extension $M/k$.

source.place: 09GT (theorem-existence-algebraic-closure), 09HC (lemma-separable-elements), 09GU (lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure), 09DT (lemma-normal-closure), 0EXM (lemma-normal-closure-galois); separable forms and exact assertions as stated by the three cited nodes.

proof.text: For finite Galois $M/k$, use strong induction on the number $n\geq1$ of terms, uniformly in all coefficients and exponents. If $n=1$, a nonzero zero gives $c_1a_1^{p^{m_1}}=0$, hence $c_1=0$, and $b_1=1$ works. For $n>1$, if some $a_j=0$, delete that term. The remaining tuple is nonzero and has $n-1\geq1$ coordinates. Apply the induction hypothesis and insert a zero in position $j$. Thus only the case in which every $a_i\ne0$ remains.

source.place: Lemma 1.12, printed p.7, induction proof; read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf; local archival copy WANTED. The arbitrary separable algebraic case is reduced to finite Galois using the existing Stacks-based nodes.

proof.text: Choose $j$ such that $m_j=\max_i m_i$. Put $x_i=a_i/a_j^{p^{m_j-m_i}}$. The denominators are nonzero, $x_j=1$, and $p^{m_j-m_i}p^{m_i}=p^{m_j}$ gives $$\sum_i c_ix_i^{p^{m_i}}=a_j^{-p^{m_j}}\sum_i c_ia_i^{p^{m_i}}=0.$$ If every $x_i$ belongs to $k$, these coordinates already give the required nonzero tuple.

source.place: Lemma 1.12, printed p.7, induction proof; read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf; local archival copy WANTED. The arbitrary separable algebraic case is reduced to finite Galois using the existing Stacks-based nodes.

proof.text: Otherwise choose $r$ with $x_r\notin k$. The extension $M/k$ is finite, separable and normal by step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] supplies $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(M/k)$ with $\sigma(x_r)\ne x_r$. Indeed, if every such automorphism fixed $x_r$, the fixed-field assertion would put $x_r$ in $k$.

source.place: 09DW, theorem-galois-theory: the base field is the fixed field of its finite Galois group.

proof.text: Let $d_i=x_i-\sigma(x_i)$. Then $d_r\ne0$ and $d_j=1-\sigma(1)=0$. The iterated Frobenius ring endomorphism of [def-weil-ring-frobenius] preserves subtraction, and $\sigma$ fixes each $c_i$, so $$\sum_i c_id_i^{p^{m_i}}=\sum_i c_ix_i^{p^{m_i}}-\sigma\!\left(\sum_i c_ix_i^{p^{m_i}}\right)=0.$$ Delete position $j$; the resulting tuple is nonzero over the same finite Galois extension and solves the equation with $n-1$ terms. The induction hypothesis gives a nonzero solution over $k$; insert a zero at $j$. This completes the induction and step 1 gives the original assertion.
